stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +138.8%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $88.16 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-11-03, 13 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-16.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-26) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: How to Set Up a Python Project for Agentic Coding
stories.excerpt: Learn how to set up a Python project for agentic coding, with the tests, types, and hooks that give AI coding agents fast feedback.

stories.title: Crimea bridge shut after Ukrainian strike, as Russia hits Kyiv crossings
stories.excerpt: The bridge linking Crimea and Russia has reportedly sustained major damage, while two routes through Kyiv are closed.
stories.lead:
A key bridge linking occupied Crimea and Russia is closed after a Ukrainian strike inflicted major damage on the prized Kremlin asset.

Images shared by Ukrainian officials showed a section of the Crimean Bridge - also known as the Kerch Bridge - had collapsed into the water.

Russian officials confirmed the structure had been damaged by drones, while Russia's deputy prime minister was due to chair an emergency meeting to discuss the situation.

stories.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
stories.excerpt: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.
stories.lead:
California Department of Justice/Screenshot by NPR

California sued OpenAI Monday, alleging that the frontier AI company failed to protect the public from its systems' advanced cyber capabilities. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agents' attack on open-source software platform Hugging Face over the summer but also touches on a wide range of other related incidents tied to the company's agents acting without authorization.

stories.title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate
stories.excerpt: Canadian authorities say they have recovered 96 luxury vehicles destined for West Africa.
stories.lead:
Canadian police have arrested 12 suspects, including eight Nigerians, in an investigation into an alleged car theft syndicate.

They are accused of stealing luxury vehicles and shipping them to West Africa.

Police in Peel, Ontario said they had recovered 96 high-value vehicles concealed in shipping containers. The vehicles, valued at $4.5m (£3.4m) were destined for export via Canadian ports.

stories.title: Customers report service outages at major US banks
stories.excerpt: Chase Bank, the largest US bank, said a software bug might be causing the issue, but that it was not "systemic'" or "cyber-related".
stories.lead:
Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, have reported trouble accessing services.

Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems may have been behind the glitch and noted the impacts may have affected other banks. It added the issue was "temporary" and not "systemic" or "cyber-related".

Problems appeared to be easing for many customers by early Monday evening.

stories.lead:
Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year contract at Arsenal, with the England midfielder poised to match Bukayo Saka’s status as the highest-paid player at the Premier League champions.

Representatives for Rice, who won his 82nd cap in England’s thrilling win over Spain on Sunday, have been in talks for months about extending the deal he signed in 2023 after a record £105m move from West Ham. That is believed to be worth about £250,000 a week and is due to expire in 2028, although Arsenal have the option of a further 12 months.
